problem:
Let $V={R}^{3}$ be the vector space equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x,y⟩={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+5{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.
$$

If $x=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -5 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
worked_solution:
Since $x$ and $y$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+5{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =(-3)\cdot 5+5\cdot ((-5)\cdot 3)+2\cdot (k\cdot 5) \\  & =-15-75+10k \\  & =-90+10k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨x,y⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & =0 \\ -90+10k & =0 \\ 10k & =90 \\ k & =9\end{aligned}
$$
